newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Saurer reiterates sees good 1997 prospects.
newsitem.headline: Saurer reiterates sees good 1997 prospects.

text.p: Swiss textile machinery and automobile component maker Saurer AG repeated comments from March that it saw good prospects for 1997 despite a weak start.

"After a rather weak first quarter, we expect on the basis of orders on hand and delivery plans that positive earnings developments will continue in the second quarter as well as the second half of the year," it said in a letter to shareholders.

It said good responses from customers who have tested its new spinning machine were cause for special optimism. It will be introduced in stages from the end of 1997 and should lead to lasting earnings growth in this division from 1998, it said.

"Chances are good that the strong market positions of all Saurer divisions, measures already adopted and the remaining potential to optimise (operations) will lead to a further increase in earnings power for the group," it said.
"The groundwork had been laid, but there is still a great deal of work ahead of us," it added.

As reported, Saurer has proposed paying back shareholders 15 Swiss francs per share. It said this stemmed from improved 1996 earnings, the group's solid finances and the promising outlook for the next few years.
